title: Three companies building the tech to grow crops on the moon
summary: Three companies are developing technology to grow crops on the moon, highlighting a shift in focus from traditional space hardware to sustainable lunar agriculture. This effort aligns with NASA's Artemis program aimed at returning humans to the moon.

title: Rocket Lab launches 8th iQPS satellite
summary: Rocket Lab successfully launched its 8th iQPS radar-imaging satellite for Japan on August 6, following a previous launch attempt that was aborted over a month earlier.

title: Chinese launch startup Orienspace targets IPO, secures funding for reusable Gravity-2 rocket
summary: Chinese commercial launch company Orienspace is preparing for an IPO while securing funding to accelerate development of its reusable Gravity-2 rocket. The Shandong-based startup aims to advance its space launch capabilities.

title: NASA and Roscosmos continue seat barter agreement
summary: NASA and Roscosmos have extended their seat barter agreement for crew exchanges between Soyuz and Crew Dragon spacecraft. However, this agreement does not currently include Boeing's Starliner.

title: New Glenn explosion linked to rocket engine valve
summary: Blue Origin identified a valve in the BE-4 engine as the cause of the New Glenn rocket's explosion during a static-fire test in May. The investigation highlights a technical issue in the rocket's propulsion system.

title: Capella, Iceye and Umbra win NRO radar-data contracts
summary: The National Reconnaissance Office awarded contracts to Capella Space, Iceye U.S., and Umbra to provide commercial synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data. This expands the U.S. government's access to radar-based Earth observation capabilities.

title: Finding room in Starlink’s shadow
summary: New communications satellite constellations are entering non-geostationary orbit (NGSO) but face challenges competing with established giants like Starlink. The article explores the viability of newcomers in the shadow of industry leaders.

title: Satellite manufacturing thrives in California despite cost and regulatory pressures
summary: Muon Space's new satellite manufacturing facility in San Jose, California, was inaugurated with support from state, local, and military representatives. The event highlights the thriving satellite manufacturing sector in California despite challenges like cost and regulatory pressures.

title: Think tank warns Europe’s orbital compute gap is widening
summary: A think tank warns that Europe's orbital computing capabilities are falling behind due to accelerated developments by U.S. companies and China's government-led initiatives. The European Space Policy Institute highlights the risk of Europe becoming dependent on foreign orbital computing infrastructure.

title: Neuraspace raises $18 million to expand sovereign space awareness
summary: Neuraspace, a Portuguese space traffic management startup, secured $18 million in funding to enhance European space domain awareness and defense capabilities.

title: SpaceX’s Falcon 9 wasn't the first rocket to crash into the moon. Here's a rundown
summary: The SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket's upper stage collided with the moon, marking the latest in a series of lunar impacts. This event highlights the growing issue of space debris and its unintended consequences.

title: Plan your perfect 2026 total solar eclipse experience with these smartphone apps
summary: Smartphone apps are being developed to help users plan for the 2026 total solar eclipse, providing exact timings and cloud cover warnings. This initiative highlights the intersection of technology and astronomy for public engagement.

title: Where will the total solar eclipse 2026 be visible from?
summary: The total solar eclipse on August 12, 2026, will be visible from parts of the Arctic, Greenland, Iceland, and northern Spain. Other regions, including parts of North America, Europe, and Africa, will experience a partial solar eclipse.

title: 'Warhammer 40,000' animated series coming to Prime Video, with Henry Cavill onboard as executive producer
summary: A 'Warhammer 40,000' animated series is set to debut on Prime Video, with Henry Cavill serving as executive producer. The series is a spinoff of the 2024 'Secret Level' anthology.

title: The 'Dark Matter' season 2 trailer is here, and it looks like Apple TV has another sci-fi hit on its hands
summary: Apple TV's 'Dark Matter' season 2 trailer has been released, showcasing another potential sci-fi hit. The trailer highlights the show's central theme of a powerful, mysterious box.

title: A SpaceX rocket just crashed into the moon. Now, the race is on to get a look at the impact site
summary: A SpaceX rocket crashed into the moon at high speed, and lunar orbiters are now racing to observe the impact site.

title: Astronomers witness the strange final moments of a massive star's supernova death (video)
summary: Astronomers captured the unusual supernova death of a massive star from its initial faint X-ray flash. This observation provides new insights into the final moments of stellar evolution.

title: Curiosity rover spots mysterious honeycombs on Mars | Space photo of the day for Aug. 5, 2026
summary: NASA's Curiosity Mars rover discovered unusual honeycomb-shaped formations in the Martian soil while exploring a large valley. The discovery adds to the rover's ongoing mission to study the Red Planet's geology and potential for past habitability.

title: On this day in space! Aug. 5, 2011:  NASA's Juno spacecraft launches to Jupiter
summary: NASA launched the Juno spacecraft on Aug. 5, 2011, to study Jupiter. The mission aimed to provide insights into the planet's composition, gravity field, and magnetic field.

title: Mars dust is toxic. How will future astronauts deal with it?
summary: Mars dust contains carcinogens like silica and heavy metals, posing health risks to future astronauts. Mitigation strategies are needed to protect human explorers on the Red Planet.

title: Crew-13 pilot reflects on career, training, and upcoming science ahead of flight to ISS
summary: NASA has moved up the launch date for the Crew-13 mission to the ISS. A pilot reflects on their career, training, and upcoming scientific objectives ahead of the flight.

title: While SpaceX recovers Ship 40, Ship 41 prepares for testing ahead of Flight 14
summary: SpaceX is recovering Ship 40 after its soft landing in the Indian Ocean, while Ship 41 prepares for testing ahead of Flight 14.

title: Launch Preview: Starlink, AST SpaceMobile, and Chinese missions fill launch manifest
summary: The first week of August is expected to be busy with multiple launches, including Starlink, AST SpaceMobile, and Chinese missions. The schedule highlights the growing activity in the space industry.

title: Boeing’s Starliner set for potential 2026 cargo run to ISS
summary: Boeing's CST-100 Starliner spacecraft may conduct a cargo mission to the International Space Station in 2026, following ongoing redesign efforts. CEO Kelly Ortberg highlighted the progress and potential timeline for the spacecraft's next mission.

title: Starbase Pad 1 Retrofits Progress as Block 3 Flights Start
summary: SpaceX has completed two flights from the newly designed Pad 2 at Starbase while retrofitting work continues on Pad 1. The upgrades are part of preparations for Block 3 flights.

title: Blue Origin continues rebuilding LC-36, prepares testing alternatives for New Glenn second stage
summary: Blue Origin is continuing to rebuild Launch Complex 36 (LC-36) and exploring alternative testing methods for the second stage of its New Glenn rocket following a recent pad explosion during a static fire test.

title: Ship 40’s flawless flight promotes next mission catch potential
summary: Ship 40 successfully completed its mission and returned intact during SpaceX's Starship Flight 13, paving the way for future missions. The flawless flight highlights potential for next mission catch operations.

title: Launch Preview: Falcon 9 and Chang Zheng rockets set to launch this week
summary: Five orbital launches are scheduled this week, including a Chang Zheng 6A rocket in China. A Falcon 9 rocket is also set to launch as part of the planned missions.

title: Juno reveals surprising subsurface tempertures at Io, remarkably smooth surface
summary: NASA's Juno spacecraft reveals surprising subsurface temperatures and a remarkably smooth surface on Jupiter's moon Io following two flybys. The findings challenge previous assumptions about the volcanic moon's geology.

title: Blue Origin to conduct New Glenn second stage hot fires on Stennis B-2 stand
summary: NASA and Blue Origin have finalized plans to conduct hot-fire tests for the second stage of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket at the Stennis B-2 test stand. This marks a significant step in the development and preparation for the rocket's upcoming missions.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: ESA celebrates 50 years with a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements. The publication marks five decades of the European Space Agency's contributions to space exploration.

title: Your chance to run software in deep space on ESA's asteroid mission
summary: The European Space Agency is inviting European researchers and companies to run their software on the Hera mission, a deep space asteroid mission. This offers a unique opportunity to test software in deep space millions of kilometers away.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A drone carrying a student-developed radar retroreflector technology successfully completed its first test flight at ESTEC, the European Space Agency’s technical centre in the Netherlands.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will use a coronagraph to study the Sun's corona by blocking out the Sun's disk, simulating an eclipse. This involves two satellites playing a 'hide and seek' game to achieve precise alignment.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event on 16–17 September at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands will bring together startup companies and Europe’s space industry to exchange ideas, showcase capabilities, and explore collaboration opportunities.

title: The silicon brains steering next-generation antennas
summary: The article discusses advancements in silicon-based technologies for next-generation antennas, highlighting their role in steering and enhancing antenna performance. This innovation is crucial for improving communication systems in the space industry.

title: Plato's electronics ready for space
summary: ESA's PLATO spacecraft has completed key electromagnetic compatibility tests in the Maxwell Test Chamber at ESTEC, confirming its electronics are space-ready. The mission is now cleared for launch on an Ariane 6 rocket in March 2027.

title: Test firing at brand new green chemical propulsion lab
summary: A new green chemical propulsion lab has conducted its first test firing. This marks a significant step in developing environmentally friendly propulsion technologies for space missions.

title: Endeavor Optical Networks Emerges from Stealth
summary: Endeavor Optical Networks has come out of stealth mode to develop a constellation of optical communications satellites. The company aims to advance space-based data transmission capabilities.

title: Rocket Lab Wins $397M Contract to Build and Launch Threat-Tracking ‘Flatellites’
summary: Rocket Lab secured a $397 million contract to develop and launch 'Flatellites' for threat-tracking. This deal highlights Rocket Lab's vertical integration strategy in the space industry.

title: SpaceX Reports Q2 Earnings
summary: SpaceX released its Q2 earnings after its record-breaking June IPO, with headline figures exceeding expectations.

title: Neuraspace Raises €15.6M to Scale its SDA Service
summary: Neuraspace has secured €15.6 million in funding to expand its Space Domain Awareness (SDA) services. The investment comes as the growing number of satellites in orbit heightens the importance of space for global defense.

title: FL Governor Candidate Launches Space Race Policy
summary: A Florida gubernatorial candidate has unveiled a new space policy aimed at securing launches, investments, and high-paying jobs for the state. The policy seeks to compete with other states and countries in the growing space industry.

title: Xona Clears Final Regulatory Hurdle for PNT Constellation
summary: Xona Space Systems has received FCC approval to broadcast Pulsar navigation signals from a full satellite constellation, marking the final regulatory hurdle before scaling deployment.

title: Kreios Taps Kongsberg NanoAvionics for 2028 VLEO Demo
summary: Kreios has selected Kongsberg NanoAvionics to support its 2028 Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) demonstration mission, which aims to test an Atmospheric-Breathing Electric Propulsion (ABEP) thruster across various altitudes below Low Earth Orbit (LEO).

title: True Anomaly Chases an Evading Target
summary: True Anomaly announced it successfully completed the first in-space pursuit of an evading target as part of the VICTUS HAZE mission. The company achieved this milestone, marking a significant advancement in space operations.

title: AFRL Adds $11.7M to Blue Origin’s Point-to-Point Cargo Contract
summary: AFRL increased Blue Origin's contract by $11.7M to study point-to-point cargo delivery using its launcher. The funding aims to explore the launcher's potential for rapid logistics missions.

title: K2 Space Raises $500M Series D at $6.8B Valuation
summary: K2 Space raised $500 million in a Series D funding round, valuing the company at $6.8 billion. This brings K2 Space's total financing to over $1 billion since 2022.

title: Capella, Iceye US, and Umbra Receive NRO Commercial SAR Contracts
summary: Capella Space, Iceye US, and Umbra have received sole source contracts from the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) for commercial synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery under the Radar Commercial Augmentation (RCA) program.

title: SpaceX Outlines Starlink Mobile Plans in First Earnings Report
summary: SpaceX reported $7.8 billion in revenue for Q2, nearly doubling year-over-year, and outlined plans for Starlink Mobile in its first earnings report. The company also set a $100 billion annual recurring revenue target.

title: Viasat Previews ViaSat-3 Satellites Entering Service in Q1 Results
summary: Viasat reported flat revenue of $1.2 billion in Q1 2027 results and previewed the entry into service of its ViaSat-3 satellites.

title: Space Force Awards Additional SB-AMTI Contracts, Including One To Rocket Lab
summary: The U.S. Space Force awarded $615 million in contracts for Space Based Airborne Moving Target Indication (SB-AMTI) to Rocket Lab, STR LLC, and others under Other Transaction Authority. This includes a contract specifically awarded to Rocket Lab.

title: L3Harris Confirms Successful Deployment for First Perimeter Truss Reflector on ViaSat-3
summary: L3Harris Technologies successfully deployed its first perimeter truss reflector on the ViaSat-3 Flight 3 satellite, which was launched by SpaceX in late April. This marks the third deployment in Viasat’s ViaSat-3 series.

title: Kreios Space to Demo Air-breathing Electric Propulsion in VLEO With NanoAvionics
summary: Kreios Space will demonstrate an air-breathing electric propulsion (ABEP) system in Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) using a spacecraft bus provided by Kongsberg NanoAvionics. This marks a significant step in advancing propulsion technology for sustained operations in VLEO.

title: Telesat Expands Lightspeed Constellation for Arctic Military Satcom Program
summary: Telesat secured a $1.9 billion contract with the Canadian government to expand its Lightspeed constellation by 69 satellites for Arctic military satcom connectivity.

title: Endeavor Optical Networks Emerges From Stealth to Build Optical MEO Data Transfer
summary: Endeavor Optical Networks has come out of stealth mode to develop an optical satellite network in Medium-Earth Orbit (MEO) for space-based data transfer. The startup aims to leverage optical communication technology for enhanced data transmission capabilities.

title: Airbus and Thales Alenia Space to Build SpainSat NG-III
summary: Airbus and Thales Alenia Space have been contracted by Hisdesat to build the SpainSat NG-III secure satellite communications satellite for Spain. Airbus will serve as the prime contractor for this project.

title: ETL Acquires Software Developer Amphinicy Technologies
summary: ETL Systems has acquired Amphinicy Technologies, a software developer specializing in satcom and Earth Observation markets. The acquisition aims to enhance ETL's ability to address complex ground segment challenges.
